# The labels a text style may be given, and what CommonMark makes of each one.
#
# `markdown` — CommonMark reads a complete construct in it: emphasis, code or a link,
# and so must both halves.
# `text` — it does not: the label is ordinary text, and neither half may hold it.
#
# Both halves of the suite hold a label that is Markdown and draw one that is text,
# and the rules for what CommonMark calls a construct are CommonMark's own: a
# delimiter run that opens an emphasis may not be followed by whitespace, and one
# that closes it may not be preceded by whitespace. `tools/compare-label-patterns.php`
# reads both halves' rules out of their own sources and runs this list through them.
#
# The verdicts are what the reference parser makes of the label: `markdown` when
# league/commonmark reads emphasis, code or a link in it, `text` when it does not.
#
# The last two markers are where the halves' rules differ from CommonMark's, and they
# are recorded so that a change to either half's rules has to say what it does about
# them: `markdown-only` is a label CommonMark reads as Markdown and neither half
# holds, `text-only` is one neither half should hold and both do.

# Strong emphasis.
markdown **Bakery**
markdown **Bakery** is open
markdown A **Bakery** here
markdown **Bakery** and **Coffee**
markdown ***Bakery***
markdown **a*b**
markdown ***a* b***
markdown **Bakery***
markdown *Bakery**

# Emphasis with one asterisk.
markdown *Bakery*
markdown A *Bakery* here
markdown (*Bakery*)
markdown a*b*c
markdown 2 *3* 4
markdown *foo* bar *baz*
markdown **Bakery** *Coffee**

# Emphasis with two underscores.
markdown __Bakery__
markdown A __Bakery__ here
markdown (__Bakery__)
markdown __Bakery__ and __Coffee__

# Emphasis with one underscore.
markdown _Bakery_
markdown A _Bakery_ here
markdown (_Bakery_)
markdown a _Bakery_ b
markdown _foo_ bar _baz_

# Code and links.
markdown `code`
markdown A `code span` here
markdown [text](url)
markdown A [link](https://example.com) here
markdown [text](url "title")

# A delimiter that opens an emphasis may not be followed by whitespace.
text ** Bakery**
text __ Bakery__
text * Bakery*
text _ Bakery_
text **Bakery **
text __Bakery __
text *Bakery *
text _Bakery _
text ** Bakery **
text __ Bakery __

# A delimiter that closes an emphasis may not be preceded by whitespace.
text __Bakery __
text *Bakery *
text _Bakery _

# A delimiter run that is not closed.
text *Bakery
text Bakery*
text _Bakery
text Bakery_
text **Bakery
text Bakery**
text `code
text [text](url

# An underscore does not open an emphasis inside a word.
text snake_case
text snake_case_name
text a_b_c
text x_Bakery_
text x_Bakery_ here
text a__b__c

# A marker on its own, and a pair of them.
text *
text _
text **
text __
text `
text * *
text _ _
text ``

# Brackets on their own are not a link.
text [Bakery]
text [Bakery
text Bakery]
text Bakery](url)

# GFM's strikethrough is not CommonMark's, and a label is plain text.
text ~~Bakery~~

# Ordinary text.
text Bakery
text Baking bread
text 50% off
text a * b * c
text 2 * 3
text a_b
text a*b

# A run of three underscores is emphasis to CommonMark and text to both halves.
markdown-only ___Bakery___
markdown-only _Bakery__
markdown-only __Bakery_ __

# A run of one asterisk and a run of two is text to CommonMark and Markdown to both.
text-only a *Bakery**a
text-only a *Bakery_*a
